entries.9.10: "All of you are versed in the duties enjoined by scripture and well acquainted with the ways of the world. Prescribe, therefore, the religious observance by which expiation may be made."
entries.10.32: Thus Rsyasringa of great splendour dwelt there with his wife Shanta, honoured with every desire fulfilled.
entries.11.2: "There will be born in the line of the Ikshvaku kings a highly righteous king named Dasaratha, auspicious and true to his word."
entries.13.10: "Let hundreds of fair lodgings be prepared for the brahmins, well appointed and furnished with abundant food and drink."
entries.13.11.1: "Let there be stables for horses and elephants, sleeping quarters, and great dwellings for the soldiers and for those lodging from abroad."
entries.14.58: Having heard his sweet speech, that composed and great-souled lord of kings bowed to him, was filled with the utmost joy, and spoke once again to Rsyasringa.
entries.15.27: "Cast off your fear, blessings upon you. For your welfare I shall slay in battle the cruel and evil-souled Ravana, terror of gods and sages, together with his sons and grandsons, his ministers, his friends, kinsmen and allies."
entries.15.28: "For ten thousand years and ten hundred more he has tormented the three worlds; slaying him, I shall set them free."
entries.20.16: "There is a rakshasa named Ravana, born in the illustrious line of Pulastya, of great strength and great prowess, attended by many rakshasas. Having received a boon from Brahma, he grievously afflicts the three worlds."
entries.21.2: "Having first promised the thing, you now wish to break your word. This breach is unworthy of the Raghus and a reversal for this house."
entries.21.18.1: "By that power, Raghava, nothing that has been or is to be remains unknown to this foremost of sages, the great-souled knower of dharma."
entries.22.7.1: No mean pair, blazing with splendour, blameless and making all fair about them, the two followed after him as the Ashvins follow the Grandsire.
entries.30.25: "I have attained my end, mighty-armed one. By you the word of your teacher has been fulfilled, and this Siddhashrama, O hero of great renown, has been made true to its name." Having thus praised Rama, he performed the twilight rite with the two of them.
entries.36.21: "Since your union was prevented when you desired a son, you shall beget no offspring upon your own wives."
entries.37.6: "Whatever the daughter of the mountain has said, that shall come to pass: you shall bear no progeny among your wives. Her word is unfailing, and this is certain beyond doubt."
entries.40.30: "Then, Kakutstha, by the immeasurable and great-souled Kapila, all the sons of Sagara were reduced to heaps of ash."
entries.45.2.1: "As we two pondered this whole tale of yours in full, scorcher of foes, the night has passed as though it were but a moment."
entries.49.7: "The ram, once gelded, will give you the greatest satisfaction, and so will those men who make such offerings for your delight."
entries.61.2: "This great obstruction has arisen in the southern quarter. We shall go to another region and there perform our austerities."
entries.61.23: Then the royal sage Ambarisha, of great splendour and great renown, set Shunahshepa in his chariot in haste and went swiftly on his way.
entries.62.9: "The time has come for that very purpose for which parents desiring auspiciousness beget sons — for their own wellbeing in the worlds beyond."
entries.68.20: The counsellors, together with all the great sages, said, "So be it." And the king, well pleased, said to his counsellors, "Tomorrow we set out."
entries.68.21: The counsellors of the lord of men, most highly honoured and endowed with every virtue, passed the night in rejoicing.
entries.70.44: "Of kings pure from the founding of their line, most righteous, born in the house of Ikshvaku, heroes and truthful of speech —
entries.70.45: "— on behalf of Rama and Lakshmana I ask for your two daughters, O king. Best of men, you should give the two who are their match to two who are theirs."
entries.77.22.1: The best of men went with Shatrughna and with his mothers; and Yudhajit, having obtained Bharata along with Shatrughna, was greatly delighted.
entries.77.31: United with that best of royal maidens who loved him, the mighty son of the royal sage, Rama, filled with joy, shone exceedingly, as Vishnu the lord of the immortals shines with Shri.
